gaps.sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
gaps.explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.

gaps.sentence: You should get that rash ___ (look at) by a doctor.
gaps.explanation: Causative 'get something done': get + object + past participle (looked at).

gaps.sentence: The results ___ (publish) on the university website next Friday.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle. 'Next Friday' fixes the future reference.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ (say) to be on the verge of bankruptcy.
gaps.explanation: It is said that... → The company is said to be... Present simple passive: is said.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is too fragile ___ (handle) without gloves.
gaps.explanation: Passive to-infinitive: to be + past participle. The manuscript receives the handling.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ (reach) by road until 1962; only mules could make the climb.
gaps.explanation: 'Until 1962' describes a past state of affairs: could not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: Her memoir ___ (translate) into fourteen languages so far.
gaps.explanation: 'So far' requires present perfect passive: has been + translated (singular 'memoir').

gaps.sentence: The manuscript might ___ if you keep touching it with bare hands.
gaps.explanation: Get + past participle (get damaged) is an informal passive common with mishaps.
